title: Before your first breath, before your first problem, He was there
subtitle: The First, before whom there is nothing, and from whom every good begins
intro: Al-Awwal (الأوَّلُ) means the First: Allah existed before all things, with no beginning, and there is nothing before Him. Everything else started at a point; He did not. It matters to you because His care for you began long before you could ask for it, and He was already there before any problem you face.

root.sense: The root carries the sense of beginning and of returning to an origin. Awwal is the first in order, the one at the front. Said of Allah, it is not first in a line of others but before every line: before time, place and every created thing, with no starting point of His own.

row.title: My life started with my effort

knowing: Al-Awwal opens the four names of 57:3: the First, the Last, the Outward and the Inward. The Prophet ﷺ explained the first of them himself in a supplication reported in Sahih Muslim: You are the First, and there is nothing before You. And in Sahih al-Bukhari: Allah existed and there was nothing other than Him. {idea}Imagine before time, before space, before any thing: Allah was there{/idea}. Not in a waiting room, not alone in need of company, but perfect and complete.

Every created thing has a start. Stars, mountains, angels and you all came into being at a moment He chose. He did not. He has no cause, no origin, and nothing produced Him. The four names together surround everything: Al-Awwal and Al-Akhir in time, before and after it all; Az-Zahir and Al-Batin in reach, above and within it all. Al-Awwal is the side of beginnings.
Scholars also drew a gentle meaning from it: He is first in giving. Every good that reaches you started with Him before it passed through anyone's hands.
seeing: When Zakariyya wondered how he could have a son in old age, he was told that his Lord says: it is easy for Me, for I created you before, when you were nothing (19:9). The Quran asks every human: was there not a time when you were not even a thing worth mentioning (76:1)? You were nothing. He was there, and He decided you would be.

When Fatimah, worn out by grinding grain, asked her father ﷺ for a servant, one narration in Sahih Muslim records that he taught her a supplication instead, which includes: You are the First, nothing is before You; You are the Last, nothing is after You; You are the Outward, nothing is above You; You are the Inward, nothing is beneath You; settle our debts and free us from poverty. Before the request, five lines of knowing Him.
trusting: When a problem arrives it can feel like it came from nowhere and now owns your life. But {idea}Al-Awwal was there before the problem{/idea}, before the illness began, before the debt existed, before the person who hurt you was born. Nothing in your life starts outside His knowledge or ahead of Him. To Allah belongs the command before and after (30:4).

It also cures a quiet arrogance. {trap}We tell our story as if it began with our hard work{/trap}: my degree, my business, my savings. Rewind further. Who gave you a body before you could work, parents before you could ask, a mind before you could study? {reward}His grace came first, so you can trust it will not suddenly run out now{/reward}. The One who cared for you before you existed will not abandon you halfway.
loving: We feel a special love for whoever was kind to us first, before we had done anything to deserve it. {idea}Al-Awwal is first in that sense too{/idea}. He fed you in the womb, clothed you when you were helpless, gave you parents when you could not even recognise them. You did not start this relationship; He did. A heart that sees that cannot help returning the love.
now: You are holding the first scan of your baby, a tiny shape on grey paper, and already worrying about money, schools and the world they will grow up in. Pause. Al-Awwal knew this child before you did, and planned its provision before it had a heartbeat. You are joining care that began long before you.
old: My life began with me, and everything I have I built from scratch.
new: Al-Awwal was giving to me before I existed; everything began with Him.
try: Before sleeping tonight, read the supplication from Sahih Muslim that names Him as the First, the Last, the Outward and the Inward.

dua.text: O Allah, You are the First and there is nothing before You. You began my life with grace before I asked; complete it with grace, and let my every beginning start with You.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ called on Him by this name in his bedtime supplication in Sahih Muslim, ending with a request to settle debts and free us from poverty.

pairs.why: Together they enclose all of time: nothing before Him, nothing after Him, and everything in between under His care.
Al-Awwal exists before all things; Al-Mubdi is the One who begins creation from nothing.

faq.a: Al-Awwal means the First: Allah existed before everything, with no beginning, and there is nothing before Him. The Prophet ﷺ explained it in a supplication in Sahih Muslim: You are the First, and there is nothing before You. It appears in 57:3.

faq.q: What are the four names in Surah al-Hadid 57:3?
faq.a: Al-Awwal (the First), Al-Akhir (the Last), Az-Zahir (the Outward or Uppermost) and Al-Batin (the Inward or Nearest). The Prophet ﷺ explained them as: nothing before You, nothing after You, nothing above You, and nothing beneath You. Together they show Allah encompasses all things in time and reach.

faq.q: Does Al-Awwal mean Allah had a beginning?
faq.a: No. Al-Awwal does not mean first in a series that started somewhere. It means Allah has no beginning at all, existing before every created thing, time and place included. Everything else was brought into being by Him.
